In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,

distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via
teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the
meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 9128) from any phone, Meeting ID:
828 5223 5956 Passcode: 886077. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00
p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Planning Commission for their consideration and
included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 828 5223 5956 Passcode: 886077.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JULY 11, 2022

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274, and via teleconference pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  John Bellas, Michael Baker International
  Jennifer Wu, Michael Baker International

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 6, 2022

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JUNE 6, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

B.  2021-22 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JANUARY 1 TO JUNE 30, 2022

COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about a code compliance case, which was opened in 2018 at
address 4831 Palos Verdes Drive North for “work without permits”. Code Compliance Officer
Matthews stated that the property owner has submitted plans and is working with staff and with
Building and Safety (Willdan) to legalize the unpermitted structures.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about how the structure (shipping container) fits in with the
aesthetics of the neighborhood. Director Wahba stated that the shipping container is in the
backyard and buried in the ground; only a small portion daylights, including a door and portions
of the side of the container. The property owner has plans to convert the shipping container into
an ADU.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked for an update on 34 Santa Bella. Code Compliance Officer
Matthews stated that she has not received a response from the property owner; a second request
for a response was sent.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 11, 2022
  1
 7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220070; ADDRESS: 10 PINTO LANE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: SINA KHAJAVI; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-220071) for a 718 sq.ft. second-story addition to an
  existing single-family residence which is built over an existing attached garage

Dean Flores, Associate Planner provided a presentation on Planning Application No. 220070
summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-220070, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220071) for a 718 sq. ft. second-
story addition and balcony to an existing single-family residence which is built over and existing
attached garage, subject to the conditions of approval.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked about the current construction activity at the property. Associate
Planning Flores stated that they have active permits for a single-story addition and an ADU, which
were approved in 2020.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if any of the neighbors had issue with the proposed balcony.
Sina Khajavi, SK Architects stated that the balcony is facing the driveway and are not directed
toward any of the neighbors. He stated that the neighbors have expressed support for the project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON inquired about why this portion of the project was not part of the
original project proposal. Mr. Khajavi stated that this would be best answered by the property
owner.

COMMISSIONER LOW asked if there were conditions of approval for the first portion of the
project. Mr. Khajavi stated that there were no additional conditions aside from the standard
conditions of approval and those conditions have been met.

Ramtin Golchini, Property Owner responded to Commissioner Olson’s question and stated that
the reason that this portion of the project was not included with the original plan, was that he
realized that additional space was needed for his growing family. Mr. Golchini stated that he
obtained signatures from his neighbors in support of this project.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220070 AS PRESENTED.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler

Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission approved Planning Application No. 220070,
approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220071). There is a 20-day appeal
period by where any member of the public may appeal this project to the City Council.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220220; ADDRESS: 6 DEERHILL DRIVE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: DOMINGO OTTOLIA; DESCRIPTION: A
  request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220221) for an interior
  remodel of an existing single-family residence that also includes a 269 sq.ft. single-story
  addition, façade update including new windows, doors, and siding, and redesigning the
  roof by removing the hip-style roof and replacing it with a shed-style roof. The proposal
  also includes increasing the roof ridge height from 12’-8" to 17’-6".

Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation on Planning Application No. PA-220220
summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application PA-220200, approving a Neighborhood Determination (NC-220221) for a
269 sq. ft. single-story addition, façade update including new windows, doors, and siding, and
redesigning the roof by removing the hip-style roof and replacing it with a shed-style roof. The
proposal also includes increasing the roof ridge height from 12’-8” to 17’-6”, subject to the
conditions of approval.

COMMISSIONER OLSON expressed his concern about the size of the shed roof, which expands
across the front of the house; also, it is a metal standing seam roof and not common to the
neighborhood. He also asked if the surrounding neighbors have been contacted and made aware
of the roof.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 11, 2022
  2
 Domingo Ottolia, Architect stated the house sits about ten feet below roadway, therefore the pitch
and massing of the roof will be diminished by the siding of the existing house. Director Wahba
stated that the house is below street level; it is a departure from what is typical in the neighborhood
and the metal standing seam roofs are only recently allowed in the City. He recommended that
the applicant work with staff and suggested ideas to break up the massing of the roof.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if there are any other roofs of this style in the City. Director Wahba
stated that other shed roofs have a lower pitch and aren’t as large.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she is not so concerned with the material and rather the
scale.

COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that the scale of the house is not really changing, and they are
taking advantage of light, the view, and minimizing the roof. He found that by keeping the roof this
way, they preserve the view of the property above. He stated that there is a large tree in the front
of the house and suggested that a condition of approval be added that the foliage remain. He also
stated that it is a departure from projects in the City, but it is very well designed.

COMMISSIONER OLSON suggested adding dormers or breaking up the roof by adding different
pitch heights.

Mr. Ottolia stated that the house is linear and the roof is parallel to the street. He explained the
changes to the roofs and stated that if the roof is changed to a gable roof (for example), the front
elevation will look the same. He further explained that a shed roof is being proposed in order to
add attic vents, ducting for HVAC, and the owner would like vaulted ceilings. He also added that
this is a modest project with minimal additions.

Blake Tarrico stated that this house was built by his grandmother, and the house where his father
grew up. He stated that he has obtained signatures from 8 or 9 surrounding neighbors, including
the neighbor directly behind this property. Mr. Tarrico stated that he is set on the installation of a
metal seam roof due to its environmental benefits, fire resistance, and durability.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that the material is not an issue; rather it is the scale and style
of the roof.

Mr. Ottolia stated that the staff report notes properties with similar styles in the City.

Mr. Tarrico stated that neighbor signatures were sent to staff, but were not included as part of the
staff report. The neighbor behind him, who is most impacted, had provided a letter of support.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she is glad to hear that the owner is the third generation
returning to the City and that he brings a new perspective to the City; however, she would
appreciate that the design reflect the community.

Mr. Tarrico stated he believes that the design fits in with the equine characteristics of the City.

VICE CHAIR YOO stated that he does not have issues with the material or design, but does agree
that there should be a break in the flat line roof look.

The PLANNING COMMSSION agreed to continue PA-220220 to a date uncertain in order to
provide time for the applicant to work with staff to make changes to the roof.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220241; LOCATION: 19 BUCKSKIN LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: DAVID AND HELEN SHAW; A
  request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220242) to legalize two
  unpermitted detached accessory structures built less than 7’ away from a bridle trail. A
  Variance (V-220243) is required to consider an application for building a structure less
  than 7’ to a bridle trail per RHEMC Section 17.06.330. The proposal also includes a
  grading application (G-220244) for on-site grading greater than 3’ or 20 cubic yards of
  earth movement.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  CONTINUE PA-220241 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN.

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, JULY 11, 2022
  3
 B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220255; LOCATION: SOUTHWEST CORNER OF
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH & PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST (27305 PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274) APPLICANT: CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; A Precise Plan of Design (PPD-220256) for George F
  Canyon Nature Center Replacement Project & Initial Study with Proposed Mitigated
  Negative Declaration (ISMND) under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

Director Wahba provided a PowerPoint presentation on Planning Application No. PA-220255
summarizing the staff report.

Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission review the ISMND
prepared for the project and the Precise Plan of Design application and recommend City Council
approve both as presented herein.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he was on the subcommittee for this project in the early
stages and a large community room was being proposed at the time; he asked why there was a
departure from the original project. Director Wahba stated that it was partly due to what the
community wanted at this location, from input provided at several community meetings, and due
to the higher anticipated cost.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her excitement for this project and thanked all who
worked on this project. She stated that she appreciates that it was kept small and more of a
community hub.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN commented that the railings and walkways are too contemporary.
Director Wahba stated that the horizontal cable system with a wood cap is what they are
proposing to use. The intent is to use a material that you can see through and beyond to the
canyon, but still provide a level of security and longevity of the materials given that this is a
commercial use.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked about signage and fencing. Director Wahba stated that the
white three-rail fence will remain along the street’s edge; and the signage has not been fully
developed.

In response to COMMISSIONER CARMAN, Director Wahba stated that there will only be drought
tolerant and native plants used for the landscaping for the site.

VICE CHAIR YOO asked about the outdoor classroom and asked if it will be secure while not
operational. Director Wahba stated that there will be a gate in between the storage and the
classroom, there will be an eight-foot wall that will provide security.

COMMISSIONER LOW commented that the project looks great and will be a nice improvement.
She also stated that the more prominent signage will help identify the building.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the entry on Hitching Post is necessary. Director Wahba stated
that it is useful for buses getting in and out, traffic on Palos Verdes Drive East, and the driveway
flows more efficiently if there is more than one-way in and out.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the area at the trailhead will be paved.

Director Wahba stated that the area will not be paved and will be used for overflow parking; paving
of a small area for ADA parking space(s) compliance could be considered.

Brad Brunskill, 7 Harbor Sight Drive, asked about the ten optional parking spaces. Director Wahba
stated that this area is existing parking; however, people do not typically park in this area since
they prefer to park closer to the trail.

COMMISSIONER EDLER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE PLANNING
  APPLICATION NO. PA-220255, A PRECISE PLAN OF DESIGN (PPD-220256) FOR
  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT PROJECT & INITIAL STUDY
  WITH PROPOSED MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION (ISMND).

AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Carman, Low, Olson, Edler

Director Wahba stated that this item will likely be presented to the City Council at their meeting of
August 23, 2022.
